blocks.text: 13. Central House of Meaning and the Unfinished Teaching Room
Real-world analogue: Ancient acoustic theaters, echoing caves, calligraphy halls, interactive museums, resonant chambers, and architecture whose doors, bridges, and walls change how speech can occur.

World relation: Crafted World architecture and Open World translation. Continuity preserves rare semantic relationships, while Quiet practice protects meanings that cannot survive constant clarification.
Connection to newer locations: It forms a sound-and-language network with the Copper Canyon Chorus, Alpine Bell Pass, Bamboo Signal Sea, City of Rainward Roofs, and Karst Lantern Provinces.
Abstract or metaphorical relation: Language is not a label placed on a finished world. A command, question, promise, lie, and gift create different spaces of possible response.
